criteria.originality: Freshness of premise and twist; penalised when close to well-known works or tropes.
criteria.visual_appeal: Strength of the hook frame, signature images, and how well the story reads with no dialogue.
criteria.feasibility: Production cost: number of characters, locations, crowd shots, complex FX and simulation (water, particles, transformations).

scoring.weighted_score: originality*0.4 + visual_appeal*0.35 + feasibility*0.25, rounded to 2 decimals

concepts.title: Snail Mail
concepts.premise: A snail mail carrier with a tiny satchel is handed an urgent letter for a flower on the far side of the garden.
concepts.visual_hook: Extreme macro: a snail in a postal cap revs like a race car on the starting line of a sidewalk crack, a dandelion clock as the stopwatch.
concepts.central_conflict: The flower closes at sunset, and the snail is the slowest courier in the garden: puddles, a sprinkler and a hungry thrush stand in the way.
concepts.ending: The snail arrives just as the petals shut. The envelope opens: it is an invitation for the flower's next bloom, dated one year later. The snail was a year early.
signature_moments: Thrush shadow passing over like a plane

concepts.title: Afraid of the Dark
concepts.premise: At dusk a boy's shadow peels off the wall and flees through town, running away from the coming night.
concepts.visual_hook: A boy waves goodbye to a friend; his shadow keeps waving the other way, then sprints off.
concepts.central_conflict: Shadows vanish in darkness, so the shadow is terrified of night. The boy must catch it before the sun sets.
concepts.ending: He builds a ring of flashlights in his bedroom. The shadow returns, and now towers huge across the ceiling every night as a guardian against the boy's own fear of the dark.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + shadow, 3 locations (street, rooftops, bedroom). Shadow is a flat silhouette layer.

concepts.title: The Night Baker
concepts.premise: A baker's dough rises so much every night that the whole bakery floats into the sky; she must bake the exact right loaf weight to land by dawn.
concepts.visual_hook: A cozy bakery lifts off its foundation on a cushion of glowing dough, chimney puffing flour clouds among the stars.
concepts.central_conflict: Each loaf she bakes changes the bakery's weight; too light and it drifts into space, too heavy and it crashes onto the sleeping town.
concepts.ending: She lands perfectly at sunrise. The camera tilts up: every star in the sky is a glowing bread roll lost on earlier nights.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero, 1 main set (bakery interior + exterior sky), moderate glow FX.

concepts.title: Pocket Volcano
concepts.premise: A girl wins a thumb-sized volcano in a jar at a fair. It grows every time it gets upset.
concepts.visual_hook: A goldfish-style prize bag at a fair, but inside is a tiny smoking volcano with an angry little rumble.
concepts.central_conflict: Everything annoys it: the cat, a sneeze, the vacuum. It swells until it fills the living room.
concepts.ending: She hugs it. It shrinks, purrs, and becomes the family's winter heater. Last shot: it happily erupts popcorn.

concepts.title: The Moon's Missing Button
concepts.premise: The night sky is a giant velvet coat fastened by the moon. One night a silver button pops off and lands in a frog's pond.
concepts.visual_hook: The sky literally comes unbuttoned: a seam of daylight splits the night above a pond.
concepts.central_conflict: A frog must carry the heavy button up a heron, a windmill and a church spire before the sky falls open completely.
concepts.ending: The frog sews it back on with spider silk. The moon gratefully gives it a tiny button-moon of its own, which now glows above the frog's lily pad.

concepts.title: The Tidy Monster
concepts.premise: The monster living under a messy kid's bed is a neat freak, horrified by the chaos.
concepts.visual_hook: Two glowing eyes under a bed, then a furry hand creeps out holding a feather duster.
concepts.central_conflict: Each night the monster secretly cleans; each day the kid wrecks it again. The monster is losing its mind.
concepts.ending: The kid catches it, and instead of screaming starts making mess on purpose as a nightly 'gift'. The monster, now happy, leaves origami thank-you cranes made of socks.

concepts.title: Floor One-and-a-Half
concepts.premise: An apartment elevator gains a new button: 1½. It opens onto a miniature city living in the gap between floors.
concepts.visual_hook: Elevator doors open on a world only knee-high: tiny streets lit by fuse-box sunsets and copper-pipe rivers.
concepts.central_conflict: Workers are about to seal the gap during renovation; the girl must warn the tiny city and help it relocate.
concepts.ending: The city moves inside her dollhouse. A week later, a new button appears in the elevator: 2¾.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + crowd of tiny citizens (reusable sprite crowd), 3 locations.

concepts.title: The Cloud Shepherd
concepts.premise: A mountain girl herds fluffy sheep-shaped clouds across the sky with a long crook.
concepts.visual_hook: A shepherd girl whistles and a flock of clouds with tiny legs trots over a ridge.
concepts.central_conflict: A dark wolf-shaped storm cloud stalks the flock through the valleys.
concepts.ending: She corners the 'wolf' and discovers it is a lost sheep-cloud soaked dark with rain. She wrings it out like laundry, it turns white, and a rainbow spills from the drip.
signature_moments: Cloud flock grazing on mountain mist

concepts.title: Sock Migration
concepts.premise: Lost socks are not lost: they are migrating birds that escape from dryers and fly south every autumn.
concepts.visual_hook: A laundromat dryer door bursts open and a V-formation of socks flaps out into the sunset.
concepts.central_conflict: One small striped sock misses the flock and must cross the city alone to catch up.
concepts.ending: It reaches a tropical island covered in single socks and finds its matching partner, who had flown the year before. The final frame: a pair of socks nesting together.

concepts.title: The Clockwork Garden
concepts.premise: An old inventor builds a garden of mechanical flowers to honor his late wife's garden, which he could never keep alive.
concepts.visual_hook: Brass tulips opening with tiny gear clicks at dawn while the old man winds each one with a key.
concepts.central_conflict: A real bumblebee keeps trying to pollinate the metal flowers and is exhausted and starving; the inventor must choose between his perfect machines and the living bee.
concepts.ending: He builds the bee a tiny brass feeder and lets it be. Spring comes: real green seedlings sprout from inside the metal flower pots, planted by the bee.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 2 characters, 2 locations (garden, workshop), seasonal palette shifts reuse same set.

concepts.title: A Lighthouse for Whales
concepts.premise: An old lighthouse keeper notices a lost whale calf keeps swimming toward his beam, confusing it for its mother's glow.
concepts.visual_hook: A lighthouse beam sweeps the fog and catches a whale calf's eye shining back like a lamp.
concepts.central_conflict: The light that saves ships is drawing the calf onto the rocks; he cannot switch it off on a stormy night.
concepts.ending: He sinks a chain of lanterns underwater, building a glowing path to the open sea where the calf's mother waits. A year later a whole pod surfaces in a line, spouting in rhythm with the lighthouse beam.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 2 characters + whale pod, 2 locations, water FX heavy.

concepts.title: Gravity Hiccups
concepts.premise: Every time a boy hiccups, gravity in the room flips upside down.
concepts.visual_hook: A boy hiccups at the breakfast table; cereal, milk, dog and grandpa drop to the ceiling.
concepts.central_conflict: His hiccups won't stop on school photo day.
concepts.ending: His friends finally scare the hiccups away. Gravity stays upside down for the whole town, and the photo is taken with everyone standing on the ceiling, smiling.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Easy rotation trick on existing sets; small cast reuse.

concepts.title: The Map That Draws Itself
concepts.premise: A girl finds a blank parchment in a flea market; as she walks, ink lines appear tracing her steps, then start drawing ahead of her.
concepts.visual_hook: Ink crawling across paper like a living vine while she walks, sketching the street before she reaches it.
concepts.central_conflict: The map leads through forest, ruins and a river crossing toward an X, and it keeps drawing dangers she must avoid.
concepts.ending: The X marks her own house. In the attic she finds a box with a child's drawing of the same map, signed by her grandmother, who once walked the same path. The map adds one last line: the girl's footprints next to her grandmother's.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero, 5 locations; ink effect is a reusable overlay.

concepts.title: Puddle Diver
concepts.premise: After rain, a boy jumps into a puddle and falls through into an upside-down sky world reflected underneath.
concepts.visual_hook: Splash, and instead of getting wet the boy falls downward into clouds, with the street now hanging overhead.
concepts.central_conflict: The sun is drying the puddle, his only way back.
concepts.ending: The puddle closes; he finds another exit and pops out of his dog's water bowl at home, soaked. The dog stares, offended.

concepts.title: Hold On, Leaf
concepts.premise: Every leaf on an oak has fallen except one stubborn leaf. A squirrel becomes its only friend.
concepts.visual_hook: A bare tree in autumn wind, one bright red leaf gripping a branch like a climber on a cliff.
concepts.central_conflict: Winter storms try to tear it away while the squirrel tries to protect it.
concepts.ending: The leaf finally lets go in the first snowfall and lands in the squirrel's nest. In spring, a tiny oak sprouts from the nest, with one red leaf.

concepts.title: Toaster Dragon
concepts.premise: A family's toast keeps coming out charcoal black. Inside the toaster lives a thumb-sized dragon.
concepts.visual_hook: Toast pops up on fire, and a tiny scaly head peeks over the slot and burps a smoke ring.
concepts.central_conflict: Dad tries to evict it with a fork, a fan and a fire extinguisher; the dragon refuses to leave its warm home.
concepts.ending: The family adopts it as their toaster. The final shot: Dad lifts the kettle lid and finds a dragon egg inside.

concepts.title: The Wandering Constellation
concepts.premise: A young stargazer notices a new constellation shaped like a cat, and it moves, nightly, closer to Earth.
concepts.visual_hook: Telescope view: a cat made of stars stretches, yawns and blinks.
concepts.central_conflict: The star-cat is lost and wants to come down; the girl must build a way up before dawn erases it.
concepts.ending: She builds a ladder of kites. The star-cat climbs down and becomes a normal kitten with a glowing nose. Above, the sky now has a dark gap in the shape of a girl.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + star creature, 2 locations; star particle FX reusable.

concepts.title: Bubble Kingdom
concepts.premise: A soap bubble blown in a park contains a tiny kingdom with a castle and knights.
concepts.visual_hook: Close-up on a drifting bubble: through the rainbow film, a castle with banners waving.
concepts.central_conflict: The bubble drifts toward a cactus stand, a dog's nose and a hot barbecue.
concepts.ending: It pops on a little girl's nose, and the kingdom tumbles onto her face. She sneezes, launching them all into a brand-new, much bigger bubble.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Bubble film FX; tiny cast as crowd sprites.

concepts.title: Sandwich on the Run
concepts.premise: In a school lunchbox, a sandwich realizes what lunchtime means and escapes.
concepts.visual_hook: A lunchbox lid creaks open and a sandwich with googly olive eyes rappels out on a string of spaghetti.
concepts.central_conflict: A hungry school, a lunch bell countdown and a cafeteria full of open mouths.
concepts.ending: It hides in the teacher's lunchbox, where the teacher's sandwich joins the escape. The two fly out the window together on a paper airplane.

concepts.title: Wet Paint
concepts.premise: At night, a girl in a painting climbs out of her canvas into a dark museum.
concepts.visual_hook: A painted hand reaches out of a gilded frame, leaving glossy fingerprints on the gallery wall.
concepts.central_conflict: The longer she stays out, the more her colors drip away. She must find the sleeping guard's lost item before she fades.
concepts.ending: She returns to the frame just before dawn. The guard wakes and finds his lost coffee mug on his desk, and notices the girl in the painting is now holding a second one.

concepts.title: The Hourglass Desert
concepts.premise: A desert lies inside a colossal hourglass; at noon each day it flips, and the dunes pour into the sky.
concepts.visual_hook: A traveler watches sand dunes rise and stream upward into a glass neck in the clouds.
concepts.central_conflict: The flip will bury the only oasis village; the traveler must reach the neck of the hourglass before noon.
concepts.ending: She plants a seed in the narrow neck. A tree grows through it, jamming the glass forever at noon: the desert becomes an endless-noon oasis with a tree linking earth and sky.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + villagers, 3 locations, heavy sand FX.

concepts.title: Rust and Rain
concepts.premise: A small rusty robot terrified of rain must carry a seed to the rooftop garden of a gray city.
concepts.visual_hook: A tiny robot hiding under an umbrella made of a bottle cap while rain hammers a giant city.
concepts.central_conflict: The garden can only bloom with rain, the one thing that could seize the robot's joints.
concepts.ending: The robot plants the seed in the storm and freezes in place, rusted solid. In spring, vines and flowers grow all over it, turning it into the garden's centrepiece; one flower-covered hand waves.

concepts.title: The Dimmest Firefly
concepts.premise: A village lights its summer festival with thousands of fireflies; one firefly can barely glow.
concepts.visual_hook: A field of bright fireflies, and one weakly flickering speck that keeps getting shooed to the back.
concepts.central_conflict: A storm blows out all lanterns and the bright fireflies hide; lost children are out in the dark field.
concepts.ending: The dim firefly guides the children home. Then it keeps rising, higher and higher, until it settles in the sky: it was never a firefly, but a baby star.

concepts.title: The Giant's Contact Lens
concepts.premise: A village wakes to find a huge frozen lake overnight and goes skating. It is actually a giant's lost contact lens.
concepts.visual_hook: Villagers skating on a perfectly round, slightly domed, crystal-clear 'lake'.
concepts.central_conflict: The ground shakes: a squinting, blind-groping giant is searching for it, flattening fences.
concepts.ending: The villagers return it. The giant pops it in, sees them clearly for the first time, gasps at how tiny they are, and, for extra safety, puts on glasses too.

concepts.title: The Fog Eater
concepts.premise: In a harbor town, a shy fluffy creature eats the morning fog.
concepts.visual_hook: A cotton-candy-like creature slurping fog off the harbor like noodles.
concepts.central_conflict: The fishermen love the clear mornings, but a dry spell means no fog and the creature is starving.
concepts.ending: The town puts kettles on every rooftop. Steam rises at dawn, the creature feasts, and grows big enough to carry the town's children on its back.

concepts.title: Balloon Giraffe
concepts.premise: At a birthday party, a balloon giraffe comes alive and wants to see the real savanna.
concepts.visual_hook: A squeaky balloon giraffe stretches its neck and pops the party's piñata.
concepts.central_conflict: Everything is sharp: roses, a cactus, a hedgehog, a fork. One wrong step and it's over.
concepts.ending: It ties itself to a helium balloon and floats away, then joins a V of migrating geese heading south toward Africa.

concepts.title: Ice Cream Meteor
concepts.premise: During a heatwave, a meteor lands in a backyard. It's a friendly alien made of ice cream.
concepts.visual_hook: A sizzling crater, and in the middle a three-scoop alien waving with a wafer hand.
concepts.central_conflict: The alien is melting; the kids must keep it cold until its ship returns at night.
concepts.ending: They smuggle it home in an ice-cream truck. It beams up, and leaves a crater full of rainbow sprinkles as a thank-you.

concepts.title: Shell Village
concepts.premise: A whole village lives on the back of a gentle giant tortoise crossing the ocean. One day, the tortoise starts to dive.
concepts.visual_hook: Wide shot: rooftops, windmills and gardens on an ancient tortoise shell at sea, waves lapping at the village edge.
concepts.central_conflict: The villagers race to seal the village in a glass-bubble dome before it goes underwater, not knowing why the tortoise is diving.
concepts.ending: On the sea floor the tortoise meets another tortoise carrying its own village. The tortoises nuzzle; two villages see each other through their domes for the first time and wave.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Villager crowd, 2 main sets, water FX.

concepts.title: Gutter Voyage
concepts.premise: A girl folds a paper boat with a drawing for her grandpa, a lighthouse keeper far away, and launches it in the rain gutter.
concepts.visual_hook: A paper boat racing down a storm-drain rapid like a whitewater raft.
concepts.central_conflict: Drains, waterfalls, a curious duck and the open sea threaten the soggy boat.
concepts.ending: The boat reaches grandpa's lighthouse rocks. A week later, a paper airplane glides through the girl's window with his drawing back to her.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Boat is a prop hero, 3 locations, water FX.

concepts.title: The Late Reflection
concepts.premise: In an old barber shop, the mirror reflects everything three seconds late, and today, a reflection starts making its own choices.
concepts.visual_hook: A barber snips; three seconds later the reflection snips something completely different.
concepts.central_conflict: The barber must secretly copy the reflection's wild haircut so the customer doesn't notice.
concepts.ending: The customer loves the outrageous new hairstyle. Then the barber's reflection takes off its apron and walks out of the mirror's frame for lunch.

concepts.title: The Cactus Who Wanted a Hug
concepts.premise: A lonely little cactus in the desert desperately wants a hug.
concepts.visual_hook: A cactus with arms opened wide, as a tumbleweed rolls past and swerves to avoid it.
concepts.central_conflict: Everyone who comes close gets poked: a lizard, a balloon, a bird. The cactus is heartbroken.
concepts.ending: At dawn, a soft fog rolls over the desert and wraps it completely, a hug that can't be popped. Covered in dew, the cactus blooms its first flower.

concepts.title: The Dream Fisherman
concepts.premise: An old fisherman rows across the night sky catching glowing dream-fish and lowering them into the chimneys of sleeping children.
concepts.visual_hook: A rowboat gliding through the stars, line dipping into a glowing school of fish.
concepts.central_conflict: One night he hooks a spiky, black nightmare fish that thrashes and threatens to capsize him.
concepts.ending: He realises the nightmare fish is frightened of him. He gently lets it go; it swims down a chimney and turns into a funny, giggling goldfish in a little girl's dream.

concepts.title: Snowman Holiday
concepts.premise: A snowman sneaks into a refrigerated truck to see the beach.
concepts.visual_hook: A snowman wearing sunglasses smuggled among frozen fish crates.
concepts.central_conflict: Every moment in the sun means melting.
concepts.ending: He reaches the beach and melts into the sea. Then he evaporates, drifts to the mountains as a cloud, and snows down to rebuild himself — still wearing sunglasses.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero, 3 locations. Note: snowman-meets-summer is a familiar trope; the water-cycle ending must carry it.

concepts.title: The Runaway Words
concepts.premise: In an owl's forest library, the letters of every book suddenly peel off the pages and flutter away like moths.
concepts.visual_hook: A book opens and its ink letters lift off as a swarm of tiny black moths.
concepts.central_conflict: The owl librarian chases the swarm through the forest before every book goes blank.
concepts.ending: The words land in an empty notebook held by a tiny owlet who couldn't write yet; they arrange themselves into the owlet's very first story. The old owl puts it on the top shelf.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 2 characters, 2 locations; letter swarm FX reusable.

concepts.title: The Kite Without a String
concepts.premise: A boy's kite snaps its string and travels the world for years, collecting souvenirs on its tail.
concepts.visual_hook: A kite tail growing longer each year: a feather, a lantern ribbon, a seashell, a snowflake ornament.
concepts.central_conflict: The kite keeps trying to find its way home through storms, cities and oceans.
concepts.ending: It finally returns to the same hill and drifts down into the hands of a small child, whose father, the boy now grown, recognises it instantly.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Kite hero, many locations (montage), 2 human characters.

concepts.title: The Uphill Boulder
concepts.premise: A hiker notices a boulder that rolls uphill whenever nobody is looking.
concepts.visual_hook: The hiker turns around; the boulder is suddenly ten meters higher up the trail, perfectly still.
concepts.central_conflict: A game of 'statues' up the mountain as she tries to catch it moving.
concepts.ending: At the summit, hundreds of boulder creatures sit in a row, waiting. The sun rises, they open sleepy eyes and watch it together, and the hiker sits among them.

concepts.title: The Doorbell in the Forest
concepts.premise: Deep in the woods, a girl finds a brass doorbell fixed on a tree trunk. There is no door.
concepts.visual_hook: A shiny doorbell in moss on an old oak, glowing faintly.
concepts.central_conflict: Each press rearranges the forest: paths swap, trees bow, the way home disappears.
concepts.ending: On the third press, a tiny door opens at the roots. A mouse in a postal cap hands her a parcel with her name on it: she was expected.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 2 characters, 1 location; layered parallax trees reshuffle.

concepts.title: Weather Vane
concepts.premise: A metal rooster on a barn weather vane is desperate to turn around and see the sunset, but the wind never lets him.
concepts.visual_hook: A weather vane rooster straining its neck, grimacing against the wind.
concepts.central_conflict: A comedic battle against changing winds, a bird perched on his tail and a lightning storm.
concepts.ending: The wind finally shifts. He sees the sunset and, on the barn across the field, a metal hen weather vane who has been trying to turn around too.

concepts.title: Ocean in a Jar
concepts.premise: A boy brings home a jar of seawater; on his desk it still has waves, weather and a tiny sailing ship.
concepts.visual_hook: A glass jar on a desk with a thunderstorm raging inside and lightning flashing the bedroom.
concepts.central_conflict: The tiny ship is sinking in the tiny storm, and the boy must calm the jar without shaking it.
concepts.ending: He breathes gently on the glass and the storm clears. Through a tiny spyglass the ship's captain looks up — and the camera pulls back: the boy's room is inside a jar, on a giant desk.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + tiny ship, 1 location; water FX contained in jar.

concepts.title: The Bee Who Lost Its Buzz
concepts.premise: A bee wakes up and its buzz is gone. When it flies, it makes the wrong sounds: a bike horn, a rubber duck, a trombone.
concepts.visual_hook: A bee takes off with a loud bike-horn HONK, and the whole meadow turns to stare.
concepts.central_conflict: The hive won't let it in without the right buzz, and every attempt produces a sillier sound.
concepts.ending: It finds its buzz stuck in a honey jar and gets it back. But the other bees loved the silly sounds, and the final shot is a hive honking, squeaking and tooting in chorus.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 1 hero + reusable bee crowd, 1 location. Designed for a sound-only format.

concepts.title: The Organ Whale
concepts.premise: A huge whale with pipe-organ blowholes plays music for a coastal town's festival each year.
concepts.visual_hook: A whale surfaces and brass organ pipes rise from its back, blasting a chord into the sky.
concepts.central_conflict: This year the whale plays out of tune and sad; something is blocking a pipe.
concepts.ending: A small girl dives in and pulls out a lost brass trumpet stuck inside. The whale plays a full symphony, and lets the girl play the trumpet on top as a soloist.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Whale + girl + town crowd, water FX.

concepts.title: Canned Weather
concepts.premise: A street vending machine sells weather in cans: Snow, Breeze, Thunder, Sunshine.
concepts.visual_hook: A man on a hot day cracks a can and a private snowstorm erupts over his head.
concepts.central_conflict: The cans misfire across the street — thunder in a café, fog in a bus, hail on a wedding.
concepts.ending: He buys 'Sunshine' for his gloomy neighbor; the machine shakes and dispenses a rainbow too big to fit through the slot, which unfurls across the whole street.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Small cast, 1 street location, mixed weather FX.

concepts.title: Crown of Crows
concepts.premise: A scarecrow that scares nobody becomes best friends with the crows it was meant to frighten.
concepts.visual_hook: A scarecrow with crows on its arms, all looking politely at the camera.
concepts.central_conflict: The farmer decides to replace it with a fearsome new scarecrow and tosses the old one on the burn pile.
concepts.ending: The crows lift it into the air together and carry it to the tallest tree in the forest, where they crown it with a ring of twigs as their king.

concepts.title: Stuck in Plaid
concepts.premise: A chameleon pet plays hide and seek with a kid and gets stuck in a plaid pattern after hiding on grandma's blanket.
concepts.visual_hook: A chameleon in perfect tartan sitting on a white bathroom tile, horrified.
concepts.central_conflict: The kid tries patterns to un-stick it: polka dots, stripes, zebras, a TV test card.
concepts.ending: It finally resets. The kid starts counting again, and can't find it anywhere — until the camera reveals it's on top of the kid's head, perfectly matching their hair.

concepts.title: The Lantern Without Light
concepts.premise: At the deep-sea lantern festival, a young anglerfish's lure refuses to glow.
concepts.visual_hook: Black ocean, hundreds of glowing anglerfish lures drifting like paper lanterns — and one dark spot.
concepts.central_conflict: The festival parade needs every lantern lit; the little fish tries batteries from a shipwreck and borrowing jellyfish.
concepts.ending: A clownfish tells a silly joke; the anglerfish laughs and its lure blazes brighter than any other: it glows only with joy. The festival becomes a laughing festival.

concepts.title: The Wishing Well's Day Off
concepts.premise: An overworked wishing well tries to grant every coin's wish, and the results are absurdly literal.
concepts.visual_hook: A stone well sweating and groaning as coins rain into it like hail.
concepts.central_conflict: Wishes stack up: a boy wants 'a big dog' and gets one the size of a bus; a girl wants 'to fly' and floats off upside down.
concepts.ending: Exhausted, the well throws its own coin into itself. Final shot: the well on a beach chair in sunglasses by the sea.
concepts.feasibility_notes: Character well + several gag characters, 2 locations.

concepts.title: The Night Train of Lost Things
concepts.premise: A night train travels through the city collecting lost things — umbrellas, gloves, toys — and returns them. A teddy bear rides it looking for its child.
concepts.visual_hook: An old glowing train glides between rooftops, its carriages full of umbrellas and odd shoes.
concepts.central_conflict: The bear has ridden for years; its child has moved and grown up. The train's route is closing.
concepts.ending: At the final stop, the conductor removes her cap: she is the grown-up child, who took this job to find him. They ride the last route together.
concepts.feasibility_notes: 2 main characters, train interior + city exterior sets.

concepts.title: Picnic on Sleeping Hill
concepts.premise: A family spreads out a picnic on a soft green hill. The hill is breathing.
concepts.visual_hook: The picnic blanket rises and falls slowly, a teacup sliding back and forth.
concepts.central_conflict: The hill is a giant moss creature waking up, and the family must pack up before it stands.
concepts.ending: The creature sits up, sniffs, and looks hungrily at the basket. The family shares a mattress-sized sandwich; they picnic together on its open palm.

concepts.title: Starfish Looking Up
concepts.premise: A little starfish wants to meet the stars it was named after.
concepts.visual_hook: A starfish climbing a rock at night, stretching one arm toward the starry sky.
concepts.central_conflict: A seagull carries it higher and higher, but the stars never get closer.
concepts.ending: Back on the beach, disappointed, it watches a meteor shower. The falling stars splash into the sea and wash up as new starfish, all looking around in wonder.

concepts.title: The Invisible Pet Shop
concepts.premise: A pet shop that sells only invisible animals. A customer opens the wrong cage.
concepts.visual_hook: Paw prints appear across spilled flour on the floor of an apparently empty shop.
concepts.central_conflict: Invisible pets escape into the street: only footprints, floating leashes and nibbled sandwiches reveal them.
concepts.ending: The pets are recaptured with flour clouds. The customer thanks the shopkeeper — and we realise the shopkeeper is invisible too: only a hat and glasses floating behind the counter.
